provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: The birth of Jesus
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state where Jesus was born.
The pupils should be able to explain why Jesus is called the Saviour.

Introduction:
We have learned about God's people in the Bible. Today we will learn about the birth of Jesus.

Content:
Jesus was born in Bethlehem. Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem for the census. There was no room in the inn so Jesus was born in a manger. Jesus is called the Saviour because he came to save people from sin.

Class activity:
Act out the Bethlehem story with pupils playing Mary Joseph and the baby Jesus.

Evaluation questions:
Where was Jesus born? Why is Jesus called the Saviour? What happened at the first Christmas?

Summary:
Jesus was born in Bethlehem and he is our Saviour.

topics.title: Jesus grew in wisdom
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list places where Jesus grew.
The pupils should be able to explain how to grow like Jesus.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jesus' birth. Today we will learn about how Jesus grew up.

Content:
Jesus grew in Nazareth. He also grew in wisdom and favor with God and people. Jesus went to church with Mary and Joseph. To grow like Jesus we must read our Bible and pray every day.

Class activity:
Draw a picture of Jesus as a boy in the church.

Evaluation questions:
Where did Jesus grow? How did Jesus grow? What can you do to grow like Jesus?

Summary:
Jesus grew in wisdom and we should grow like Jesus too.

topics.title: Jesus calls his friends
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the twelve disciples.
The pupils should be able to explain how Jesus calls people.

Introduction:
We have learned about Jesus as a boy. Today we will learn about Jesus calling his friends to help him.

Content:
Jesus called twelve special friends to be his disciples. Their names were Peter Andrew James John Philip Bartholomew Thomas Matthew James Thaddaeus Simon and Judas. Jesus calls us to be his friends too by following his teachings.

Class activity:
Make a list of the twelve disciples on the board and have pupils copy it.

Evaluation questions:
Who were Jesus' twelve disciples? How did Jesus call his disciples? How does Jesus call you today?

Summary:
Jesus called twelve disciples to be his special friends and helpers.

topics.title: Jesus teaches love
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what love means.
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the good neighbour.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jesus' disciples. Today we will learn about Jesus teaching love.

Content:
Jesus taught that we should love God and love our neighbour. The story of the good neighbour is about a man who was hurt. A priest and a Levite passed by but did not help. A Samaritan man stopped and helped him. This shows we should help everyone even people who are different from us.

Class activity:
Act out the good neighbour story with pupils playing the injured man priest Levite and good Samaritan.

Evaluation questions:
What did Jesus teach about love? Who helped the hurt man in the story? How can you be a good neighbour?

Summary:
Jesus taught us to love our neighbour and help others.

topics.title: Jesus prays
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list times when Jesus prayed.
The pupils should be able to explain why prayer is important.

Introduction:
We have learned about Jesus teaching love. Today we will learn about Jesus praying.

Content:
Jesus prayed often. He prayed in the morning before he started his day. He prayed all night sometimes. He prayed before he chose his disciples. He prayed in the garden of Gethsemane. Prayer is important because it helps us talk to God and get his help.

Class activity:
Practice saying a simple prayer together as a class.

Evaluation questions:
When did Jesus pray? Why is prayer important? What do you pray about?

Summary:
Jesus prayed often and we should pray too.

topics.title: Jesus the helper
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name ways Jesus helped people.
The pupils should be able to explain how they can help others.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jesus praying. Today we will learn about Jesus helping people.

Content:
Jesus helped many people. He made blind men see. He helped a man who could not walk. He fed five thousand people with five small loaves and two fish. We can help others by sharing our toys helping classmates and being kind to everyone.

Class activity:
Draw a picture of helping someone like Jesus did.

Evaluation questions:
How did Jesus help people? How can you help others like Jesus? What happened when Jesus fed the five thousand?

Summary:
Jesus helped many people and we should help others too.

topics.title: The last supper
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to describe what happened at the last supper.
The pupils should be able to explain why we remember Jesus.

Introduction:
We have learned about Jesus helping people. Today we will learn about Jesus' last supper with his friends.

Content:
Jesus had a special meal with his disciples. This was the last supper. Jesus broke bread and said this is my body. He poured wine and said this is my blood. He told them to do this to remember him. We remember Jesus when we take communion in church.

Class activity:
Act out the last supper with pupils playing Jesus and the disciples.

Evaluation questions:
What did Jesus do at the last supper? Why do we remember Jesus? What did Jesus tell his disciples to do?

Summary:
Jesus had a last supper with his friends and told us to remember him.

topics.title: Jesus rises again
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the empty tomb.
The pupils should be able to explain why Easter is joyful.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about the last supper. Today we will learn about Jesus rising from the dead.

Content:
After Jesus died he was buried in a tomb. On the third day the tomb was empty. Jesus had risen from the dead! Mary Magdalene saw Jesus first. Easter is joyful because Jesus is alive and he gives us life forever.

Class activity:
Make an empty tomb craft with paper and stones.

Evaluation questions:
What was in the tomb on Easter morning? Who saw Jesus first after he rose? Why is Easter a happy time?

Summary:
Jesus rose from the dead and that is why we celebrate Easter with joy.

topics.title: The church is born
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state how the church started.
The pupils should be able to explain why we love the church.

Introduction:
We have learned about Jesus rising again. Today we will learn about how the church began.

Content:
After Jesus went to heaven his disciples gathered together. They prayed and waited for the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit came on the day of Pentecost. The church started with the friends of Jesus who believed in him. We love the church because it is Jesus' family on earth.

Class activity:
Draw a picture of the first church with the disciples praying together.

Evaluation questions:
How did the church start? What happened on the day of Pentecost? Why do we love the church?

Summary:
The church started with Jesus' friends and it is his family on earth.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this year.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about our lessons.

Introduction:
Today we will review all we learned this year and have a small quiz.

Content:
We learned about Jesus' birth how he grew how he called disciples how he taught love how he prayed how he helped the last supper his resurrection and the birth of the church. Let's remember these important stories.

Class activity:
Play a game where pupils line up and answer questions about what we learned this year.

Evaluation questions:
Where was Jesus born? How did Jesus teach love? What happened at the last supper? Why is Easter joyful? How did the church start?

Summary:
We reviewed all we learned this year and Jesus is our Saviour forever.
